drug_name: Ascorbic Acid and Tocopheryl Acid (Vitamin C and Vitamin E)
what_its_for: This combination supplement provides two powerful antioxidants — Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) and Vitamin E (tocopheryl acid) — that work together to help protect your body's cells from damage. They support a healthy immune system, help your skin stay healthy, assist in wound healing, and help protect your eyes, heart, and other organs from oxidative stress (cell damage caused by everyday wear and tear). Your doctor or pharmacist may recommend this supplement if you are not getting enough of these vitamins from your diet.
how_to_take: Take this supplement by mouth, exactly as directed on the label or as your doctor or pharmacist tells you. Swallow tablets or capsules whole with a full glass of water (8 ounces). If you are taking a chewable tablet, chew it completely before swallowing. If you are taking a liquid form, use the measuring device that comes with it — do not use a regular household spoon, as it may not give you the right amount. Taking this supplement with food or a meal can help reduce any stomach upset. Do not crush, break, or chew regular tablets or capsules unless your pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: The usual recommended daily doses for adults are: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid): 500 mg to 1,000 mg per day. Vitamin E (Tocopheryl): 400 IU (International Units) per day. However, your doctor or pharmacist may recommend a different dose based on your specific health needs. Do not take more than the recommended amount unless your doctor tells you to. Taking very high doses of Vitamin C (more than 2,000 mg per day) or Vitamin E (more than 1,000 IU per day) can cause unwanted side effects. Always follow the dosing instructions on your product label.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose. Missing an occasional dose of a supplement is generally not harmful, but try to take it around the same time each day to build a healthy routine.
storage: Store this supplement at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from direct light, heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom, near a sink, or in a damp area, as heat and humidity can break down the vitamins. Keep the bottle or package tightly closed when not in use. Keep all supplements out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package. If the tablets or capsules look discolored, crumbled, or smell unusual, do not use them — ask your pharmacist for a replacement.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking doses higher than recommended without talking to your doctor first, as very high amounts can cause harm. Avoid taking this supplement with antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium at the same time, as they may interact with Vitamin C. If you are taking blood thinners (such as warfarin/Coumadin), be careful, because high doses of Vitamin E may increase your risk of bleeding — always check with your doctor or pharmacist first. Avoid smoking, as it breaks down Vitamin C in your body more quickly. Limit alcohol, as it can reduce how well your body absorbs these vitamins. Avoid taking multiple vitamin supplements at the same time without checking with your pharmacist, as this can lead to getting too much of a vitamin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or pharmacist right away if you experience any of the following: Stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away. Signs of kidney stones, such as severe back or side pain, blood in your urine, or pain when urinating (this can happen with very high doses of Vitamin C). Unusual bleeding or bruising (especially if you take blood thinners). Signs of an allergic reaction, such as rash, itching, swelling of your face or throat, dizziness, or difficulty breathing. Headache, fatigue, blurred vision, or muscle weakness. Any new or unusual symptoms that concern you after starting this supplement.
when_it_works: Vitamin C and Vitamin E are absorbed into your body shortly after you take them. However, you may not notice immediate effects because these vitamins work gradually to support your overall health. If you are taking them to correct a deficiency, you may start to feel better — such as having more energy, improved skin, or faster wound healing — within a few weeks of consistent daily use. For long-term benefits like immune support and antioxidant protection, it is important to take this supplement every day as part of a healthy lifestyle. Results vary from person to person.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women: These vitamins are generally considered safe during pregnancy and breastfeeding at recommended doses. However, do not take high doses without your doctor's approval, as very large amounts of Vitamin E during pregnancy may pose risks. Always consult your doctor before taking any supplement while pregnant or nursing. Children: Do not give adult-strength doses to children. Use only children's formulations and follow the dosing on the package or as directed by your pediatrician. Older adults (65+): Older adults may benefit from these vitamins, but should be cautious with high doses of Vitamin E, especially if taking blood thinners. Consult your doctor before starting. People with kidney disease: High doses of Vitamin C can increase the risk of kidney stones. If you have kidney disease or a history of kidney stones, talk to your doctor before taking this supplement. People with certain medical conditions: If you have hemochromatosis (iron overload disorder), glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, or are on chemotherapy or radiation therapy, talk to your doctor before taking Vitamin C or Vitamin E supplements, as they may interfere with your treatment.
